guide.title: Understanding AVIF for BMP output
guide.markdown:
### What is an AVIF file?

AVIF stands for AV1 Image File Format. Its specification was written by the Alliance for Open Media, which was founded in 2015 for royalty-free media formats, and the format stores AV1-coded pictures inside a HEIF container. A file can use lossy or lossless compression, hold transparency or an image sequence, and reach twelve bits per channel for HDR and wide-gamut color. It can also carry Exif, XMP and an ICC profile. Most people meet AVIF as small images on websites.

### Programs that open AVIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - GIMP: imports and exports AVIF since version 2.10.22.
  - ImageMagick: reads AVIF files.
- **Web:**
  - Google Chrome: version 85 added AVIF decoding.
  - Mozilla Firefox: version 93 added AVIF image support.
- **Mobile:**
  - Android: AVIF decoding starts with version 12.
  - Safari: on iOS 16 it added still AVIF images.

### AVIF and BMP compared

- **Names and types**: .avif is image/avif and .bmp is image/bmp.
- **Compression**: AVIF is compact. A BMP commonly keeps its pixels raw, with an optional lossless run-length scheme, so the file is bulky.
- **Color**: a BMP stores between one and 32 bits for each pixel.
- **Use**: BMP turns up in Windows screen captures, system graphics and simple pipelines that want plain pixels.

Your browser handles the AVIF side, and ImageMagick encodes the BMP from the pixels. An animated AVIF gives frame one, and embedded metadata is left behind.

### Other ways to convert AVIF to BMP

- **GIMP:** GIMP 2.10.22 and later open AVIF. Open the file, choose File > Export As and save it as BMP. In the BMP export dialog, run-length encoding is available for indexed and grayscale images only, writing color space information is on by default and can be switched off for programs that can't read it, and an RGB format list sets the layout for other images.

### Problems with AVIF files

- **A browser shows nothing**: older browsers can fail to show AVIF, which is why sites keep a JPEG, PNG or WebP fallback. This converter also needs a browser that can decode AVIF.
- **GIMP refuses it**: releases older than 2.10.22 lack the AVIF importer.
- **Android depth**: handsets and tablets decode baseline 8-bit AVIF, and 10-bit decoding is optional.
- **Slow opening**: decoding an AVIF is slow, and encoding can take several seconds per image.

guide.title: Understanding BIN for JPEG output
guide.markdown:
### What is a BIN file?

The .bin ending marks raw binary data and says nothing about which image encoding, if any, is inside. The content could be a disc image, a dump of a program's memory or an email attachment, and the name gives no hint which. GNU objcopy, for one, can turn an object file into a flat memory image with the symbols and relocation records left out. The files people bring to a page like this are mostly pictures saved under that name, such as the ATT00001.bin attachments Outlook produces, or a Mac file in MacBinary, whose own extension is .bin.

### Programs that open BIN files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - GNU Emacs Hexl: shows and edits the bytes with hexl-find-file.
  - UltraEdit: gives a hex view of a .bin file.
- **Web:**
  - HexEd.it: inspects and edits the bytes in your browser.

A binary editor lays out the bytes in hexadecimal beside a text view. It does not interpret them as a photograph, so none of these programs shows the picture.

### BIN and JPEG compared

- **Names**: .bin has no fixed type, while .jpg and .jpeg are the same format.
- **Structure**: a BIN has no fixed layout. A JPEG is a lossy picture format built for photographs.
- **Transparency**: a JPEG cannot hold an alpha channel, so see-through pixels are lost, and it keeps no editable layers.

This page reads the start of the file and checks it against the signatures of known picture formats. A Mac file saved as MacBinary is recognized too, by skipping its 128-byte header. When the bytes match a picture, the file is converted as that format and you get a JPEG. Anything else is refused with a message that the file isn't an image, without the page reading all of it.

### Other ways to convert BIN to JPEG

This page works from the .bin itself. It identifies the picture from its first bytes, so you do not need to know beforehand whether the file is a PNG, a GIF or another picture format.

### Problems with BIN files

- **"This file isn't an image"**: the BIN contains data that is not a picture, so there is nothing to make a JPEG from.
- **Raw pixel data**: a BIN of bare pixel values has no picture header for the page to recognize, so it is refused as not an image.
- **The picture couldn't be read**: the file starts like an image but looks damaged or incomplete.
- **Editing in a hex editor**: work on a copy, because changing the wrong bytes alters the data.

guide.title: Understanding BMP for DDS output
guide.markdown:
### What is a BMP file?

BMP is the Windows Bitmap family, controlled by Microsoft and used originally on Windows and OS/2. Pixels are normally stored uncompressed, with lossless compression as an option, and you will run into the format in Windows screen captures and built-in system graphics. Version 5 appeared with Windows 98 in 1998 and can hold an ICC profile and an alpha channel. A BMP holds no vector shapes and no live typography.

### Programs that open BMP files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - ImageMagick: reads BMP images.
- **Web:**
  - Mozilla Firefox: displays BMP pictures.
  - Google Chrome: supports BMP images.

### BMP and DDS compared

- **Names and types**: .bmp is image/bmp. .dds is Microsoft's DirectDraw Surface texture format.
- **Purpose**: BMP is a plain picture. DDS is a texture container for games and GPUs.
- **Contents**: a DDS can hold raw pixels or compressed texture data, and a chain of mipmaps may accompany the largest surface. Cube maps and volume textures fit as well, and Direct3D 10 and 11 reach texture arrays by way of an extra header.

The decoding happens in your browser, and ImageMagick turns the resulting 8-bit RGBA pixels into a DDS. Neither a compression format nor a mipmap option is set, and metadata is dropped.

### Other ways to convert BMP to DDS

- **DirectXTex texconv:** run `texconv -ft dds -f BC3_UNORM texture.bmp` to choose the pixel format yourself. Here -ft names the output file type, and -f names the DXGI format. texconv reads a BMP through Windows Imaging Component, and DDS output gets a full mipmap chain unless -m sets a different number of levels.
- **ImageMagick:** run `magick surface.bmp surface.dds`. ImageMagick lists BMP and DDS as readable and writable, and its DDS notes cover DXT compression and mipmaps.

### Problems with BMP files

- **Large files**: an uncompressed BMP can be rather large, and a PNG or JPEG is more practical to share.
- **A program wants an older header**: some programs expect an older bitmap header, and ImageMagick writes those as BMP3 or BMP2.
- **No editable shapes or text**: a BMP keeps no vector shapes or live typography, so keep the project file you drew it from.

guide.title: Understanding CDR for JPEG output
guide.markdown:
### What is a CDR file?

CorelDRAW saves its drawings as CDR by default. Corel calls the format primarily vector, with shapes, text and effects, though bitmap content can live in a drawing as well. Saving can compress bitmaps and graphic objects, which reduces the file size but slows opening and saving. Properties such as a title and subject can be stored, and fonts are embedded unless they are Asian fonts or lack embedding permission. For compatibility, the Save As dialog lists earlier CDR versions.

### Programs that open CDR files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - LibreOffice Draw: opens CDR by way of the libcdr library.
- **Windows and Mac:**
  - CorelDRAW: opens its native drawings,.

### CDR and JPEG compared

- **Names**: .cdr is a proprietary Corel file, and JPEG goes by .jpg or .jpeg.
- **Structure**: a CDR holds shapes, text and pages that stay editable. A JPEG is a single flat picture and keeps no editable layers.
- **Transparency**: a JPEG can't store an alpha channel, so see-through areas are lost.

This converter cannot read CDR files. If you add a CDR, the page stops with "Image decode failed." Export the JPEG from a program that understands CorelDRAW drawings instead.

### Other ways to convert CDR to JPEG

- **CorelDRAW:** open the drawing and choose File > Export. Pick the folder, set Save as type to JPG and type a file name. Two optional check boxes limit what is exported: Export this page only, for the current page of a multipage file, and Selected only, for the selected objects. Neither is available for every format. Click Export.
- **Corel PHOTO-PAINT:** choose File > Import, pick CDR - CorelDRAW (*.cdr) in the list next to the File name box, click the filename, click Import, then click the image window. In the Convert to bitmap dialog, adjust the width, height, resolution or color mode. Then choose File > Export, pick a JPEG format in the Save as type list, type a file name and click Save.

### Problems with CDR files

- **A newer drawing won't open**: an earlier CorelDRAW release can refuse it, and the documented workaround is a copy saved for the older version.
- **Saving backward changes the drawing**: Corel warns that the copy can lose effects, change how items look or limit editing.
- **PHOTO-PAINT lost the vectors**: imported CDR files are rasterized, so shapes cannot be edited afterward.
- **Fonts**: embedding is limited by each font's permissions, and Asian fonts are not embedded, so check them before you share the CDR.

guide.title: Understanding CR2 for PDF output
guide.markdown:
### What is a CR2 file?

Canon RAW version 2, or CR2, is the raw image format of many Canon EOS cameras from the mid-2000s until CR3 replaced it. Inside a TIFF-based file sit unprocessed sensor readings and an embedded JPEG preview. The Library of Congress notes that raw formats need special software to turn them into usable images. CR2 is a proprietary Canon format, so long-term access depends on software keeping up with it.

### Programs that open CR2 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - darktable: accepts CR2 on import and decodes supported raw files with RawSpeed.
- **Windows and Mac:**
  - Canon Digital Photo Professional: supports .CR2 among the raw extensions it opens, for images from compatible cameras.
- **Linux:**
  - LibRaw dcraw_emu: a LibRaw sample that emulates dcraw and takes its options as command-line keys.

### CR2 and PDF compared

- **Names**: .cr2 is a Canon camera format. .pdf is a document format with a fixed page layout.
- **Contents**: a CR2 holds sensor data and a preview. A PDF page holds the finished picture.
- **Use**: CR2 is for editing photos. PDF is for sharing and printing.

ImageMagick, compiled to WebAssembly, reads the CR2 in your browser as one picture. In the PDF you get one page that matches the image, one pixel per point and no margin, so it is neither A4 nor Letter. The image is embedded losslessly as PNG data, and each file gets a PDF of its own. Anything over about 537 megapixels is refused as too large.

### Other ways to convert CR2 to PDF

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick cr2:review.cr2 review.pdf`. ImageMagick lists CR2 as read-only and PDF as readable and writable, and the `cr2:` prefix tells it to read the file as a CR2.

### Problems with CR2 files

- **Your camera is not supported**: Canon's Digital Photo Professional handles .CR2 images from compatible cameras only, so check that yours is one of them.
- **The page size is odd**: the PDF page matches the pixel size, so it is large on paper. Place the picture on a standard page in a layout program.
- **Long-term access**: CR2 is a proprietary format, so reading it depends on software that keeps supporting it.

guide.title: Understanding DST for SVG output
guide.markdown:
### What is a DST file?

Tajima developed DST as a machine embroidery stitch format. It stores needle positions plus machine commands: jumps, color stops and trims. It is not a picture. A machine must be told when to insert a color change, thread trim, tie off or tie in, and a DST carries those commands. It is used for industrial embroidery machines and digitized designs, and embroidery programs widely support it. A basic DST has no color information.

### Programs that open DST files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - Ink/Stitch: reads and writes DST embroidery files, and you open them as you would an SVG in Inkscape. The design opens in Manual Stitch Mode, where you can edit individual points.
- **Windows and Mac:**
  - Embrilliance Essentials: reads DST files and lets you change or remove individual colors and save a new file.
- **Web:**
  - Wilcom Library: accepts DST uploads and previews designs at true scale in a browser on Mac, PC and tablets, with a Library user license. You do not need EmbroideryStudio to use it.

### DST and SVG compared

- **Contents**: a DST has stitch coordinates and machine commands. An SVG describes shapes and paths as XML text that scales to any size.
- **Color**: a DST stores no color information, while an SVG is XML that CSS can style.
- **Use**: a DST feeds industrial embroidery machines. An SVG suits logos, illustrations and charts.

This converter cannot read DST files. A DST added here is met with "Image decode failed." Use pyembroidery in Python to write the SVG.

### Other ways to convert DST to SVG

- **pyembroidery:** run `pyembroidery.convert("sample.dst", "sample.svg")` in Python. The library reads DST and writes SVG. Its read_dst function loads a DST's stitch data, and a DST variant called extended adds a color sequence through its headers.

### Problems with DST files

- **Odd preview colors**: a DST stores no color information, so apply a threadlist, as Ink/Stitch allows, to give the design colors.
- **Resizing changes the stitching**: enlarging a basic DST spreads the same stitches apart, while shrinking it tightens the spacing and shortens the stitches.
- **Rebuilding objects**: EmbroideryStudio can try to rebuild objects from stitches, yet it cannot recreate the colors.

guide.title: Understanding DV for MP4 output
guide.markdown:
### What is a DV file?

DV is a family of digital video encodings developed for videocassettes in the early 1990s, from a specification by a ten-company consortium later standardized by IEC. Each picture is compressed on its own with a discrete cosine transform, so DV does not compress from frame to frame the way MPEG-2 does. Raw DV data can be stored as a file with a .dv or .dif extension.

### Programs that open DV files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - FFmpeg: a command-line tool that both decodes and encodes DV video.
  - VLC media player: a free and open source player with a DV demuxer registered for the .dv extension.

### DV and MP4 compared

- **Names**: .dv is a tape-based stream format. MP4 is MPEG-4 Part 14, a container for video and audio.
- **Compression**: DV compresses each picture alone. MP4 here holds H.264 with AAC audio.
- **Use**: DV is legacy camcorder footage. MP4 plays on nearly every device.

The work is done by a WebAssembly build of FFmpeg inside your browser tab. It re-encodes the video as H.264 with libx264, at the ultrafast preset with constant rate factor 32, and encodes the sound as AAC at 96 kbps. Interlaced frames get deinterlaced. The output stops at 1920 pixels on its longer side and 30 frames per second, and a smaller or slower source is never raised. Rounding costs a frame with odd dimensions one pixel. No upload takes place.

### Other ways to convert DV to MP4

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i tape.dv -c:v libx264 -c:a aac viewing.mp4`. FFmpeg lists DV video and MP4 as supported for both decoding and encoding, and the command picks H.264 video and AAC sound.

### Problems with DV files

- **Raw or wrapped**: the same DV data can sit raw in a .dv or .dif file or inside AVI, QuickTime or MXF. This page's picker takes files ending in .dv.
- **Two kinds of DV**: there is a consumer kind and a professional kind, and DVCAM from Sony and DVCPRO from Panasonic are the professional developments.
- **Frame metadata**: DV attaches metadata to every recorded frame. Your original file is left unchanged, so keep it.
- **A long file is slow**: conversion runs on your own device, so time depends on its speed.

guide.title: Understanding GIF for PSD output
guide.markdown:
### What is a GIF file?

CompuServe introduced GIF, the Graphics Interchange Format, in 1987. Images are packed losslessly with LZW, each palette tops out at 256 colors, and simple animation is part of the design: one file can carry many images, spaced by delays measured in hundredths of a second. The July 1990 GIF89a revision added transparency, per-frame delays, comments and application data blocks. Transparency means choosing a single palette color to be invisible, so partial opacity is impossible. License fees for LZW from Unisys began in 1994, and the patents expired in 2003 and 2004. You see GIF in reaction images, stickers, icons and short looping clips.

### Programs that open GIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - GIMP: can export a still picture or a layered animation.
  - ImageMagick: handles GIF input.
- **Web:**
  - Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox: display GIF.
- **Mobile:**
  - Safari and Chrome: display GIF on a phone.

### GIF and PSD compared

- **Names and types**: .gif is image/gif. .psd is Photoshop's native document, image/vnd.adobe.photoshop.
- **Color**: a GIF frame is capped at 256 palette entries. A PSD header lists one, eight, 16 and 32 bits as possible sample depths.
- **Structure**: a PSD keeps layers, masks and image resources in separate sections. A GIF holds frames.
- **Compression**: a PSD stores pixel data raw or encoded with RLE or ZIP, while GIF uses LZW.
- **Limit**: a PSD side can be no longer than 30,000 pixels, and PSB removes that cap.

Your browser decodes the GIF, and only its first frame is kept, so an animated GIF gives one still picture. The pixels pass through 8-bit RGBA, and ImageMagick writes the PSD. The page builds no layers and no animation frames.

### Other ways to convert GIF to PSD

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick sticker.gif sticker.psd` in a terminal. ImageMagick lists GIF and PSD as readable and writable.

### Problems with GIF files

- **Comments can drop out**: GIMP leaves out a GIF comment that uses characters beyond plain seven-bit text.
- **Soft edges look hard**: a GIF cannot retain partial opacity.
- **Banding**: a GIF holds at most 256 colors, so gradients can shift, and the PSD cannot restore the missing shades.
- **Later frames look partial**: frame disposal changes how later images cover earlier ones.

guide.title: Understanding GIF for SWF output
guide.markdown:
### What is a GIF file?

GIF dates to 1987 and CompuServe. Its GIF89a revision of July 1990 introduced transparency, animation timing, comments and application blocks. Compression is lossless LZW, but every image has a palette of 256 colors at most. Many images in one file, separated by delays in hundredths of a second, make a GIF animate. The media type is image/gif, and every major browser displays it.

### Programs that open GIF files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - GIMP: writes still pictures or multilayer animations as GIF.
  - ImageMagick: supports reading GIF.
- **Web:**
  - Google Chrome and Mozilla Firefox: show GIF in a tab.
- **Mobile:**
  - Safari and Chrome: handle GIF on a phone.

### GIF and SWF compared

- **Names and types**: .gif is image/gif. SWF has the media type application/vnd.adobe.flash.movie.
- **Color**: GIF frames use palettes capped at 256 colors, while the SWF here carries video.
- **Sound**: a GIF is silent. SWF can carry audio, but the file made here has none.
- **Animation**: GIF repeats a stack of images. A SWF is a timeline-based legacy format that can also hold vector graphics and bitmap video.

Shockwave Flash started at Macromedia, which Adobe acquired in 2005, and carried Flash animations, games and interactive content with ActionScript behind them. Adobe Flash Player reached end of life on 31 December 2020. This page makes a video SWF, so no ActionScript is added.

In your browser, FFmpeg runs as WebAssembly and chooses the video codec itself: its default for SWF is Sorenson Spark (FLV1) video at 200 kbit/s. Interlaced frames are deinterlaced, and the picture is capped at 1920 pixels and 30 frames per second, with each side trimmed to an even value.

### Other ways to convert GIF to SWF

- **FFmpeg:** run `ffmpeg -i badge.gif -an -c:v flv badge.swf`. The `-an` option skips audio, and `-c:v` selects the video encoder. FFmpeg lists GIF and SWF as both readable and writable.
- **SWFTools gif2swf:** run `gif2swf -o badge.swf badge.gif`. The `-o` option sets the name of the SWF output file, and the GIF is the input file.

### Problems with GIF files

- **Banding in gradients**: a GIF is limited to 256 colors, which changes smooth gradients.
- **Frames overlay wrongly**: disposal settings decide how later images sit over earlier ones.
- **Comments can drop out**: an export from GIMP skips a GIF comment holding characters outside the seven-bit range.
- **Large GIFs**: a long, large GIF becomes many video frames, so conversion takes longer on a slow device.

guide.title: Understanding JP2 for JPEG output
guide.markdown:
### What is a JP2 file?

JP2 wraps a JPEG 2000 codestream in the Part 1 file format, developed by the Joint Photographic Experts Group. JPEG 2000 compression can be lossy or lossless, and the codestream inside decides which, not the wrapper. The wrapper can store color profiles, opacity information and other metadata. A JP2 reader ignores wrapper extensions it does not understand. Its standard extension is .jp2 and its registered media type is image/jp2. The Library of Congress serves digitized maps and newspapers as lossy JP2 images.

### Programs that open JP2 files

- **Windows, Mac and Linux:**
  - ImageMagick: lists read and write support for JP2.
  - OpenJPEG: an open-source JPEG 2000 codec written in C.
- **Windows and Mac:**
  - Adobe Photoshop: opens a JP2 file when you select it in the latest version.

### JP2 and JPEG compared

- **Names**: .jp2 is image/jp2; JPEG uses .jpg or .jpeg.
- **Compression**: JPEG 2000 allows lossy or lossless coding, while JPEG is lossy.
- **Opacity**: a JP2 may store opacity, which JPEG cannot hold because it has no alpha transparency.
- **Metadata**: the JP2 wrapper can carry color profiles and other metadata alongside the picture.
- **Use**: JP2 suits archives and service images, while JPEG is used for web photographs, camera output and email attachments.
- **After converting**: open the JPEG and compare it with the JP2, since a lossy JPEG cannot return to the original and the JP2 should be kept.

The JP2 is opened as a single picture by ImageMagick running inside your browser tab, and the page sets no JPEG quality. The page refuses a file larger than about 537 megapixels.

### Other ways to convert JP2 to JPEG

- **ImageMagick:** run `magick scan.jp2 shared.jpeg`. ImageMagick lists JP2 and JPEG as readable and writable.

### Problems with JP2 files

- **JPX is not JP2**: the JPX variant belongs to Part 2 of JPEG 2000, not the basic wrapper of Part 1.
- **Browsers do not decode it**: the Library of Congress notes that browsers do not natively decode JPEG 2000, so JP2 files are often converted to a web-friendly format.
- **Few cameras write it**: most cameras do not encode JPEG 2000, so a JP2 is rarely straight out of a camera.
